ephemeris.title: VSOP87A streamed heliocentric planet ephemeris (ecliptic and equinox J2000)

source.theory: Bretagnon and Francou, Planetary theories in rectangular and spherical variables: VSOP87 solutions, Astronomy and Astrophysics 202 (1988), 309-315
source.credit: VSOP87 theory by Pierre Bretagnon and Gerard Francou; JavaScript implementation by G.C. Marty

sampling.note: One-Julian-day keyframes from VSOP87A (heliocentric rectangular, ecliptic and equinox J2000; the earlier build used VSOP87C, which is referred to the ecliptic of date and drifted about 50 arcseconds a year from the J2000 star frame). The runtime interpolates with cubic Hermite segments whose tangents are central differences, removing the up-to-6,000 km chord error of linear interpolation. Orbit paths are representative display guides sampled across one nominal period about J2000 and are not osculating elements.

limitations: This browser asset is a bounded visualization ephemeris, not an operational navigation product. It samples VSOP87A daily from 1975 to 2050, omits Pluto, and does not include covariance, light-time, relativity corrections beyond the source theory, Earth orientation or current JPL/INPOP fitting. Pluto uses Astronomy Engine. File and format names keep their original 'vsop87c' spelling for compatibility.
